q: 1. Bitumen felt is used for .....
explain: Bitumen felt is used both as a water-proofing layer (roofs) and as a damp-proof course.

q: 2. Duco paints are .....
explain: Duco is a trade name for nitro-cellulose lacquer paint, i.e. a cellulose paint.

q: 3. The most commonly used base for timber painting, is .....
explain: White lead is the most common base for painting woodwork.

q: 4. The most important constituent of varnish, is
explain: Resin is the essential film-forming ingredient of varnish, giving it its glossy, protective finish.

q: 5. Turpentine oil is used in paints as .....
explain: Turpentine is a volatile liquid used as a thinner, which evaporates after the paint is applied.

q: 6. Linseed oil is used in paints as .....
explain: Linseed oil is a drying oil that acts as the vehicle (carrier) for pigment, forming a film when it dries.

q: 7. The most fire resistant paint are
explain: Asbestos paints are the most fire resistant because asbestos itself is a non-combustible mineral fiber.

q: 8. Plastic bitumen is generally used for
explain: Being pliable, plastic bitumen is well suited to filling cracks and small gaps in construction.

q: 9. Fracture of asbestos is
explain: Asbestos is unique for its fibrous structure, meaning it breaks into long, thin, flexible fibers rather than shards.

q: 10. Bitumen paints offer .....
explain: Bitumen paints give a black protective, water-resistant coating rather than a decorative one.

q: 11. The most important constituent of varnish, is .....
explain: As per the answer key, option d. Note: resin is generally the key ingredient of varnish, so the key answer is debatable.

q: 12. The functions of a base in oil paint are
options: it makes the film of the paint hard, durable and more resistant to abrasion
it gets oxidized in drying and forms a thin, tough, adhesive, durable and water proofing film
it provides gloss to the painted surface
explain: The base (typically a metallic oxide) provides body to the paint, giving the film hardness, durability, and abrasion resistance.

q: 13. The small area on painted surface enclosed by hairline cracks are known as
explain: Crazing refers to fine hairline cracks that form a network of small enclosed areas on a painted surface.

q: 14. The liquid medium used in enamel paints is .....
explain: Enamel paint is made by mixing pigment (white lead or zinc white) in varnish.

q: 15. The metallic oxide used in the form of powder in a paint is called .....
explain: The base is a metallic oxide in powder form, such as white lead, zinc oxide or titanium white.

q: 16. ...... tar is produced by distillation of bituminous shales.
explain: Mineral tar is produced specifically from the distillation of bituminous shale rock.

q: 17. Asphalt is a
options: mixture of bitumen and inert material
explain: Asphalt is essentially a mixture of bitumen combined with inert mineral matter (sand, limestone, etc.).

q: 18. Regarding solubility of asphalt, it is soluble in
explain: Since asphalt contains inert mineral matter along with bitumen, it dissolves only partially in carbon disulphide, unlike pure bitumen.

q: 19. The specific gravity of bitumen is
explain: Bitumen typically has a specific gravity of around 1.0 to 1.09, slightly denser than water.

q: 20. The amount of water used for one kilograms distemper is
explain: Approximately 0.6 litre of water is typically used to mix with 1 kg of distemper powder.

q: 21. What indicates for 80/100 in case of bitumen?
options: Penetration residue from loss on heating of bitumen
explain: The 80/100 notation refers to the penetration grade, indicating the depth (in tenths of mm) a needle penetrates the bitumen sample under standard conditions.

q: 22. The ingredient which gives the desired colour to a paint is called
explain: Pigments are finely ground solid particles that provide color, opacity, and some level of protection in paint.

q: 23. The function of base of an oil paint is
options: to form the body of the paint
to reinforce the film of the paint after drying
to prevent penetration of paint to lower surfaces
explain: The 'base' (like white lead or zinc oxide) provides the bulk or body of the paint and determines its character.

q: 24. The vehicle used in case of enamel paints is
explain: As per key but Enamel paint is essentially a mixture of pigment and varnish, which gives it a hard, glossy finish.

q: 25. The main component of oil paint is
explain: Oil paint requires a base/pigment, a vehicle (carrier), and a thinner (like turpentine) to be effective.

q: 26. Base pigments are used for
explain: The base is a solid substance in a fine state of division and forms the bulk of a paint. It imparts durability and protects the surface from weathering.

q: 27. Extenders used in paints for
explain: Extenders (or fillers) are added to paint to increase its volume and make it spread more easily, which helps in reducing the overall cost.

q: 28. Vehicle not used in paint is
explain: Turpentine oil is a thinner, not a vehicle (carrier oil). Linseed, poppy, and tung oils are all common vehicles.

q: 29. Bitumen 80/100 indicates
options: Penetration of residue from loss on heating
explain: The 80/100 designation specifies the penetration grade of bitumen, a measure of its hardness/consistency.

q: 30. Distemper paint means
explain: Distemper is fundamentally a water-based paint made from chalk, pigment, and a glue/water binder.

q: 31. The painting work is generally specified by
explain: In engineering estimates, painting work is measured and specified in terms of surface area (square meters/feet).

q: 32. Snowcem is
explain: Snowcem is a well-known commercial brand name for waterproof cement-based paint.

q: 33. The pigment commonly used in the manufacture
explain: Ambers (browns), Iron Oxide (reds/browns), and Lamp Black (blacks) are all standard pigments used to provide color to paint.

q: 34. Muller is concerned with
explain: A muller is a tool (often stone) used to grind and mix pigments with a vehicle during paint preparation.

q: 35. Stucco paints are suitable for
explain: Stucco paints are specifically designed for external masonry surfaces like stone and brick.

q: 36. The radiator of vehicles are pointed with
explain: Bronze or aluminum paints are used for radiators due to their high thermal conductivity and heat resistance.

q: 37. Plastic asphalt is
options: a mixture of cement and asphalt
explain: Plastic asphalt is typically a mixture of asphalt and cement used for patching and waterproofing.
